title: Valkyria Chronicles III
subtitle: The war follows soldiers without names
summary: Valkyria Chronicles III is Sega and Media.Vision's PSP tactical role-playing game, released in Japan on 27 January 2011. Its story runs alongside the original Valkyria Chronicles, following the Nameless, a penal military unit assigned dangerous operations during Gallia's war. body: Valkyria Chronicles III is Sega and Media.Vision's PSP tactical role-playing game, released in Japan on 27 January 2011. Its story runs alongside the original Valkyria Chronicles, following the Nameless, a penal military unit assigned dangerous operations during Gallia's war. The viewpoint changes the campaign's meaning: the player commands soldiers whose place within the army is already precarious. The series' combination of tactical planning and directly controlled movement remains, but the story concentrates on a smaller group fighting through work that others prefer to leave unacknowledged. Familiar history becomes another set of personal circumstances.

The player distributes actions across the unit, then controls a selected soldier while moving, taking cover and attacking. Decisions made from the tactical view are tested by the route actually taken through enemy fire. The group must be developed across the campaign, making its abilities part of planning for the next assignment. The format carries forward work from Valkyria Chronicles II while adjusting the systems for this different cast. The player has to connect a larger operational plan to the limited distance and immediate dangers one soldier can manage at a time.

Takeshi Ozawa returned as director, with Raita Honjou providing character designs and Hitoshi Sakimoto composing the music. The opening theme was performed by May'n. An expanded edition followed in November 2011, but the game was not officially localised after the preceding PSP title's limited sales. A fan translation for that expanded release appeared in 2014. Valkyria Chronicles III remains a distinctive parallel story within the series, using the same broad war to ask what it looks like from a unit whose members have been stripped of their ordinary military identities.
